newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Cheap power a boon for mine projects in new Congo.
newsitem.headline: Cheap power a boon for mine projects in new Congo.

text.p: Laurent Kabila's new Congo has ample, cheap electricity to power its mining projects, analysts and investors said on Friday.
"Power is there and it's seriously cheap," John Clemmow, investment banker at South Africa's Investec bank, told Reuters.
Former Zaire's power supply is mostly supplied by the Inga hydro-electric power station, which is situated on the Congo river in the north of the country.
The Inga-Shaba power line is 1,800 kilometres long and runs from Inga to the southern, mineral-rich Katanga Province, formerly called Shaba.

According to Richard Garnett, director of America Mineral Fields Inc, a company developing two large mining projects in the country, only two percent of the new Congo's population have electricity in their homes.

"Here there is a tremendous over-capacity of power supply and a lot of the turbines at the Inga hydro-elecric facility are standing idle. One of the benefits of (former Zaire) is that there is actually an abundance of electrical power," Garnett said.
In April Laurent Kabila's rebel alliance awarded AMF the right to develop the Kipushi zinc mine as well as the Kolwezi copper/cobalt tailings project, 300 kilometres northwest of Lubumbashi.
Kabila ousted the regime of Mobutu Sese Seko last month.
